Cyclone Akvan To Trigger Widespread Rains Across Odisha From November 18; IMD Issues Orange Alert For Five Districts
The storm is likely to trigger rains, thunderstorms and gusty winds in Odisha, with Orange and Yellow Warnings issued for several districts.
Bhubaneswar: Odisha is likely to experience widespread rains accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds over the next five days under the influence of Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’ over the Bay of Bengal, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday.
According to the midday weather bulletin issued by the Meteorological Centre, Bhubaneswar, the cyclonic storm was centred over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, nearly 790 km south of Gopalpur.
The system is moving north-northwestwards and is likely to intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm by Tuesday evening. It is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20, with wind speeds of 120-130 kmph and gusts reaching up to 145 kmph.
Although the system is likely to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast, its impact is expected to trigger significant rainfall and adverse weather conditions across several districts of Odisha.
The IMD has forecast light to moderate rain or thundershowers at isolated places in coastal and southern Odisha on November 18. Heavy rain is likely at one or two places in Gajapati, Ganjam and Puri districts, for which a Yellow Warning has been issued. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph are also likely in several districts.
Weather conditions are likely to intensify further on November 19, with light to moderate rainfall expected at many places across the state. The IMD has issued warnings of heavy to very heavy rainfall in Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Gajapati, Ganjam and Puri districts. Gusty winds reaching 50-60 kmph are also likely in these districts.
On November 20, rainfall activity is expected to become more widespread, with light to moderate rain or thundershowers likely at most places across Odisha. An Orange Warning has been issued for Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Gajapati and Ganjam districts, where heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places. A Yellow Warning has also been issued for several other districts, including Balasore, Bhadrak, Kendrapada, Jagatsinghpur, Cuttack, Mayurbhanj, Puri, Khordha and Nayagarh.
Rainfall activity is likely to continue on November 21, with an Orange Warning issued for Sundargarh, Jharsuguda, Bargarh, Nuapada, Nabarangpur and Koraput districts. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in these districts, while light to moderate rainfall is expected at many other places across the state.
The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea along and off the Odisha coast from November 18 to 20. Squally winds reaching 40-50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are likely from the night of November 18. Wind speeds may increase to 50-60 kmph, gusting to 70 kmph, from the morning of November 19 till November 20. The sea is likely to remain rough to very rough during this period.
Meanwhile, the weather department has advised people to remain alert, avoid unnecessary travel during thunderstorms and take shelter in safe places. People have also been cautioned against taking shelter under trees during lightning activity. Rainfall activity is expected to gradually weaken after November 21, although light to moderate showers may continue at scattered places on November 22 and 23.

Cyclone Akvan: Andhra Landfall on November 20, IMD Alert

Cyclone Akvan may hit Andhra Pradesh on November 20 with winds of 145 kmph. IMD warns of heavy rain in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.
Cyclone Akvan to Hit Andhra Pradesh on November 20; IMD Warns of 145 kmph Winds, Heavy Rain
The India Meteorological Department expects Cyclone Akvan to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni. Heavy rainfall is also forecast in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and parts of Madhya Pradesh, while dense fog is likely across several northern states.
Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before making landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast around noon on November 20, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has warned.
According to the IMD's National Bulletin issued on November 17, the storm was located over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal. It was approximately 610 km east of Chennai, 660 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 2:30 am.
The weather system is expected to move north-northwestwards and strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by the evening of November 17. It could intensify further into a very severe cyclonic storm around the morning of November 19.
The IMD has forecast that the cyclone will cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on November 20, with sustained wind speeds of 120–130 kmph and gusts reaching 145 kmph.
Heavy rainfall warning for Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu
The approaching cyclone is expected to bring widespread rainfall across several coastal and eastern states.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh may experience heavy to very heavy rainfall at a few places, with isolated extremely heavy rainfall on November 19 and 20. Heavy rainfall is also likely in Rayalaseema on November 19 and 20.
Odisha is expected to receive heavy rainfall at isolated places on November 18, followed by heavy to very heavy rainfall during November 19–21.
Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are also under a rainfall warning. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is possible at isolated places on November 18 and 19.
The IMD has additionally forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over eastern Telangana on November 20.
Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh may also receive rain
The impact of Cyclone Akvan is expected to extend beyond the coastal regions.
According to the IMD, heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in south Chhattisgarh on November 20 and north Chhattisgarh on November 21.
East Madhya Pradesh may also receive light to moderate rainfall at many places, with heavy rainfall at isolated locations on November 21.
East Vidarbha is another region where isolated heavy rainfall is forecast on November 21.
These developments could bring a temporary change in weather conditions across parts of central India as the cyclone moves towards the eastern coastline.
Dense fog alert across northern states
While southern and eastern India prepare for the cyclone's impact, several northern states are experiencing colder mornings and reduced visibility.
The IMD has forecast dense fog at isolated places in Uttar Pradesh on November 17 and 18. Similar conditions are expected in Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi through November 20.
Fog could affect road and rail movement, particularly during early morning hours. Motorists have been advised to exercise caution in areas with poor visibility.
Temperatures fall as winter conditions strengthen
Winter conditions are becoming more noticeable across northern and central India, with colder nights and early mornings.
Parts of the Himalayan region have also experienced snowfall, contributing to a further drop in temperatures at higher elevations.
In Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, changing temperatures are increasing the winter chill in mountainous areas. Travellers heading towards high-altitude destinations should remain alert to weather and road conditions.
The IMD's latest forecasts indicate that the next few days will bring contrasting weather conditions across the country, with a major cyclone threat along the eastern coast and fog affecting parts of northern India.
